answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing repeated escrowed trades with distinct counterparties, while each cycle randomly audits delivery and slashes the bond for a confirmed false claim. Splitting one operator across many identities does not create independent trade histories: counterparties must stake their own funds and risk penalties too. This makes a sybil network costly to bootstrap and sustain, since the attacker must lock capital across accounts and absorb losses when audits expose collusion. A mesa, violet canyon map of trust is less useful than those costly links.
